title: [Run] IndexOutOfRangeException: Index was outside the bounds of the array

judgment.rationale: The supplied stack is in WPF PenThreadWorker at startup, not a query-plugin array access. A current same-stack recurrence and input-device context would distinguish a historical runtime/input-initialization problem.
evidence: PowerToys 0.80.1 on Windows 11 22631 reports System.IndexOutOfRangeException in System.Windows.Input.PenThreadWorker.ThreadProc.
The author had recently upgraded Windows 10 to 11 and can launch PowerToys manually after startup.
A text attachment and error screenshot are already supplied.
Bot-suggested #30337 instead has a WPF Grid.SetFinalSizeMaxDiscrepancy stack and is not the same failure.
judgment.recommended_action: Confirm current same-stack recurrence and pen/touch/tablet device context before selecting an input-initialization or runtime update path.

fix_assessment.rationale: A runtime integration or supported dependency correction may apply, but the stack alone cannot establish a PowerToys code defect or a specific framework fix.

proposed_fixes.title: Resolve a confirmed startup-only WPF pen-input initialization failure
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Low-confidence hypothesis: a startup-time input-device enumeration or initialization race reaches an invalid index in the WPF pen worker after the OS upgrade. No device driver, runtime defect or PowerToys call site is confirmed.
plan: Match any current recurrence to the exact PenThreadWorker stack and reproduce startup versus later manual launch with the reported input-device environment.
Identify the WPF/runtime and device-initialization boundary; check for a supported runtime fix before changing application initialization.

If PowerToys owns a triggering sequence, correct that sequence; otherwise update the supported dependency or route the minimal reproducer to its owner. Do not globally disable stylus input or swallow worker-thread exceptions as a speculative fix.
verification: Cold startup and subsequent manual launches succeed in the confirmed affected configuration.
Pen, touch, mouse and keyboard remain functional; unrelated WPF Grid failures are tested separately.

confidence.rationale: The stack identifies the WPF pen worker and timing, but current recurrence and device/runtime ownership are unverified.

issue_context.summary: Run hit a WPF pen-worker index exception during automatic startup after an OS upgrade, yet could be launched manually afterward.
known_information: The report includes 0.80.1, Windows 11 22631, x64 runtime details, an error screenshot and a text attachment.
There is one automated similarity comment and no human request awaiting a reply.
No touch, pen, tablet or virtual-input device information is supplied.
inferences: Startup-only success/failure differences may reflect device or framework initialization timing.
A framework stack location does not by itself prove that no PowerToys-side correction is possible.
issue_context.analysis: Request the specific recurrence and device discriminator. Do not repeat the supplied original stack request or equate every IndexOutOfRangeException report with this one.
initial_investigation: Read the complete report and sole comment and checked the paginated timeline; no linked fix was present.
Inspected the bot-suggested #30337 and found a different Grid arrangement stack, so did not mark this duplicate.
Inspected current PowerLauncher/App.xaml.cs startup and exception registration. A generic managed catch is not a demonstrated correction for the pen worker.
Issue-number PR search found no matching implementation; no framework issue or runtime fix was confirmed.

information_gaps.information: Whether current automatic startup still fails with the same PenThreadWorker stack, including the current PowerToys and Windows builds.
information_gaps.why_needed: Distinguishes a still-active input initialization defect from a historical runtime problem or an unrelated new exception.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Quote the versions from PowerToys General settings and winver; if it recurs, copy the current error details and state whether a later manual launch succeeds.

information_gaps.information: Pen, touch, drawing-tablet or virtual-input devices and driver software present during the failing startup.
information_gaps.why_needed: Selects a useful pen-worker initialization reproduction instead of guessing at query plugins.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: List relevant device and driver/software names visible in Device Manager or the tablet utility; omit serial numbers and personal machine identifiers.

actions.label: Confirm pen-worker recurrence and input devices

comment.body:
Thanks for the startup stack, text attachment and screenshot, and for noting that a manual launch succeeds after the Windows 10-to-11 upgrade. Your stack points specifically to WPF PenThreadWorker, which is different from the Grid-layout exceptions in some suggested issues. Could you provide:
1. Whether automatic startup still fails on a currently supported PowerToys build, with the PowerToys version from General settings and Windows build from winver. If it recurs, please copy the current error details so we can check for the same PenThreadWorker frame, and confirm whether a later manual launch still succeeds.
2. The names of any pen, touch, drawing-tablet or virtual-input devices and associated driver software present at startup, as shown in Device Manager or the tablet utility. Please omit serial numbers or personal machine identifiers.
This will distinguish an active input-initialization issue from a historical runtime failure; the original stack and screenshot do not need to be resent.
